extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and litigators (attorneys who file or defend IPRs before the PTAB, and appellate counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating whether the PTAB should exercise its discretion to deny institution of an inter partes review under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a), centered on the six Fintiv factors and related case developments. Useful for petitioners, patent owners, and counsel preparing filings or arguing discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic assessment of efficiency, fairness, and merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fintiv factors relate to whether efficiency, fairness, and the merits support the exercise of discretionary denial by the PTAB; the Board takes a holistic view and recognizes overlap among factors so some facts may be relevant to more than one factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are instructed to consider all factors together rather than mechanically; note that overlap exists between factors and that particular facts can affect multiple factors. Parties should present facts across factors (including timing, stays, investments, overlap, and merits) to show how the balance favors or disfavors discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 1 — Whether the court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted if a proceeding is instituted
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether a district court has granted a stay of the litigation, or whether specific evidence indicates a stay is likely if an IPR is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A district court stay pending PTAB trial (or an ITC trial) strongly weighs against exercising discretionary denial because it allays concerns of inefficiency and duplication. A denial of a motion to stay (absent indication the court might reconsider if PTAB instituted) can weigh in favor of denial. If no stay motion has been requested or granted, this factor is neutral unless there is case-specific evidence; the Board will not speculate about how a district court will rule absent specific evidence. Parties should submit specific stay-related evidence if available; absence of such evidence generally leaves this factor neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 2 — Proximity of the court’s trial date to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for a Final Written Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Examines timing between a district court's scheduled trial date and the PTAB's projected Final Written Decision (FWD) date (the PTAB must issue a FWD within one year after institution under 35 U.S.C. §316(a)(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the court's trial is earlier than the PTAB's projected FWD, this often weighs in favor of discretionary denial (risk of duplicative efforts/conflicting decisions). If the trial is at/around or after the projected FWD, other factors become more important. Panels differ on how to treat uncertainty in trial dates: some take court schedules at face value absent strong contrary evidence, others treat repeated schedule changes or qualifiers as reducing weight. The Board may focus on the proximity to the FWD as a proxy for the likelihood the district court will reach validity issues before the PTAB. Parties should provide evidence if trial dates are uncertain or likely to move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 3 — Investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers the amount and type of substantive work already completed in the parallel litigation by the court and the parties at the time of the institution decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive orders (e.g., preliminary injunctions, detailed claim construction/Markman orders) and other significant investments weigh in favor of denying institution. The Board measures this investment at the time of institution. A key countervailing consideration is petitioner's diligence in filing: prompt filing after becoming aware of asserted claims may weigh against denial; late filings (e.g., around the time patent owner responded to invalidity contentions) may weigh for denial. Panels may also consider practical burdens (e.g., many patents/claims challenged across multiple petitions, office closures affecting preparation). Parties should explain timing and reasons for filing dates and provide detail on substantive orders to justify weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 4 — Overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Explores the extent to which claims, grounds, arguments, and evidence in the petition overlap with those in the district court litigation, as overlap raises concerns of inefficiency and conflicting decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial or identical overlap of claims/grounds/evidence strongly favors discretionary denial. Overlap is highly fact-dependent. Petitioners can mitigate overlap concerns by stipulations (e.g., agreeing not to pursue the same grounds in district court if IPR is instituted). The PTAB has noted that broader stipulations (e.g., not pursuing any ground that could reasonably have been raised in an IPR under §102/§103 based on patents/printed publications) are more persuasive and can tip this factor toward permitting institution. Parties should consider and propose appropriate stipulations and explain the scope of overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 5 — Whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses whether the petitioner before the PTAB is also a defendant in the related district court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the petitioner is the same as the district court defendant, panels have generally treated this factor as weighing in favor of discretionary denial (concerns about litigating the same issues twice). If the district court litigation is stayed pending IPR, the factor may be neutral or only slightly favor denial. There are divergent views (some judges view the factor as neutral when parties are identical). Parties should explain party identities and any stays to clarify the factor's weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 6 — Other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch-all for other relevant circumstances the Board may consider, including the relative merits of the petition and any other case-specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board invites parties to point out particular strengths or weaknesses of the petition to help the Board decide whether merits tip the balance. Examples of arguments under this factor include the presence of parallel petitions (some panels find parallel petitions do not favor denial), the number of times a patent has been asserted or previously challenged, and other case-specific considerations. Parties should expressly address merits and any other unique circumstances that could influence the Board’s discretion.
